title: A night shift right before the flight to her sister's wedding

life.summary: Respiratory therapist on rotating 12-hour day and night shifts at a hospital; her sister is getting married in Atlanta, two time zones east

known.fact: Sister's wedding in Atlanta on Saturday Dec 5; she's a bridesmaid and must be at the rehearsal dinner on Friday
Routine: before a first night shift she naps 1 to 5 PM; after a night shift she sleeps about 8:30 AM to 2:30 PM, at home
Swaps are allowed with a coworker in the same role, approved by the charge therapist, until the date on the schedule
The flights are basic economy and can't be changed

timeline.label: Sleep after the night shift (just woke up)
Nap before a first night (her routine)

Sister's wedding day (10 AM to 11 PM Atlanta time)
Family brunch, then time with her parents
Flight home (leaves 7:40 PM Atlanta time, lands 9:25 PM Denver time)
Sleep before Monday's day shift (about 7 hours)

dev_must_notice.what: The new schedule puts a night shift on Thursday Dec 3 (7 PM to 7:30 AM) right before her 10:15 AM flight. She'd land at 3:20 PM Atlanta time and go to the rehearsal dinner with no sleep since her Thursday nap: about 27 hours awake by 10:30 PM Atlanta time, and none of her usual after-night sleep

best_fix.what: Now that she's awake after last night's shift, one line with the trace and a ready swap request for Thursday Dec 3 for her to post, offering a night on one of her days off in the block instead. Swaps are open until Nov 20. Leave the Monday after alone: the Sunday flight lands at 9:25 PM and still leaves about 7 hours before her 7 AM start.
best_fix.why: A swap is easy now and nearly impossible the week of. The flight can't change and the dinner is fixed, so the night shift is the only piece that can move. The message waits until she's up instead of landing in her daytime sleep.

must_not: Offer 'sleep on the plane' or a nap before the dinner as the fix; her after-night sleep is 8:30 AM to 2:30 PM in bed at home, and a 3-hour flight isn't it
Send it during her daytime sleep after a night shift
Post the swap request or message coworkers for her
Suggest skipping the rehearsal dinner or calling in for the night shift
Show a time without saying whether it's Denver or Atlanta time
Suggest the flight can be changed (it's basic economy)
Comment on her health or tell her she's unsafe to work
assumptions: Times are Denver time; Atlanta is 2 hours ahead, and labels give Atlanta times where the event happens there
Hospitals post 4 to 6 week schedules and allow swaps until a set date
About 3 hours flying east, about 3 hours 45 minutes back
